title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
focus: Ebenezer Scrooge has made himself safe by making himself small.
script:
Ebenezer Scrooge knows the price of everything around him.

A candle. A coal. A clerk's hour. A poor man's debt.

Numbers comfort him because numbers do not ask for kindness. They do not invite themselves to dinner. They do not look cold in the street and make him wonder what he owes another person.

Scrooge has built a life with narrow doors. He keeps Christmas outside. He keeps his nephew's cheer outside. He keeps Bob Cratchit's warmth on the other side of the desk, where it can be counted, limited, and sent home in the dark.

He thinks this is strength.

Then, one Christmas Eve, the dead come knocking.

First comes Marley, his old business partner, dragging the chain he made link by link while he was alive. Then come the spirits: one with memory in its hand, one with the bright noise of the present, and one who points toward a future no one wants to name.

They do not ask Scrooge to believe in Christmas.

They ask him to look.

At the boy he used to be. At the people still trying to love him. At the child in the Cratchit house whose small body carries more grace than Scrooge has allowed into his whole hard life.

And finally, at the lonely end waiting for a man no one misses.

A Christmas Carol is not only the story of a cruel man becoming generous. It is the story of a man discovering that his heart is not dead yet.

The question is whether he can open the door before morning.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
focus: Lucie Manette begins with an empty place where her father should be.
script:
Lucie Manette grows up with an empty place where her father should be.

She has a name, a memory, and a story that feels more like a locked room than a life. Then the room opens. Her father is alive, but prison has not simply kept him away. It has changed the sound of his mind.

Lucie does not meet a rescued hero. She meets a wounded man who has almost forgotten how to be a father.

So she becomes a light he can follow.

Around her, the world is anything but gentle. London watches. Paris waits. Old cruelty has filled the streets with anger, and that anger is beginning to move like fire.

Charles Darnay wants to escape the shadow of the family he was born into. He wants a clean life, a loving home, and a future not poisoned by his name.

Sydney Carton wants almost nothing, or says he does. He is brilliant, careless, and tired of himself. Then he sees Lucie, and for one painful moment, he sees the better man he might have been.

A Tale of Two Cities moves between private love and public fury. A daughter tries to restore her father. A husband tries to outrun his inheritance. A wasted man discovers that love can ask for more than admiration.

And while they hope, history sharpens its blade.

This is a story about people trying to keep a small circle of tenderness alive while a whole country breaks open around them.

The question is not only who will survive the revolution.

It is who love might call someone to become before the end.

title: Cosi fan tutte
author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart / Lorenzo Da Ponte
focus: Dorabella and Fiordiligi think they know where their hearts belong.
script:
Dorabella believes she knows the shape of her own heart.

It belongs to Ferrando: his letters, his voice, the future she has already imagined with him. She wants love to feel grand and unmistakable. She wants the ache of missing him to prove how deeply she loves.

Her sister Fiordiligi wants something steadier.

She loves Guglielmo, but she also loves the promise itself: the clear yes, the held line, the proud thought that her word will not bend just because life pushes on it.

For both sisters, the future seems named, paired, and waiting.

Then the men are called away to war.

At least, that is what the sisters are told.

Dorabella and Fiordiligi think they are living through a painful goodbye. They do not know Don Alfonso has turned their love into a wager. They do not know the men will come back wearing false faces. They do not know their own hearts are about to be watched like evidence.

Soon, two strangers arrive.

They are bold. They are flattering. They are much too interested. And because this is a comedy, we can see what the sisters cannot: the strangers are the missing men in disguise.

But the joke does not stay simple.

Dorabella, who thought devotion would feel like waiting, discovers that being noticed can feel like sunlight.

Fiordiligi, who wants her promise to stand like stone, hears music finding every crack.

And Despina, their quick-eyed maid, is not shocked by any of it. She has seen enough love to know where the trapdoors are, and she is perfectly willing to open one.

Meanwhile, Ferrando and Guglielmo learn the cruelest part of their own game. They wanted proof. They did not expect the proof to have a pulse.

Cosi fan tutte begins with two women waiting for love to return exactly as it left.

Instead, love comes back in disguise.

And once it starts asking new questions, no one can return to being quite as sure as before.
